headline: Nvidia and Japan to build 140MW AI factory with 27,500 GPUs
summary: The facility will train open multimodal foundation models for robotics, digital twins, and industrial automation.
details: Nvidia and Japan's Noetra Corp. are building a 140-megawatt AI factory with 27,500 Rubin GPUs and 13,750 Vera CPUs. The facility will be built from Vera Rubin NVL72 racks on Nvidia's DSX reference platform, connected with Spectrum-X Ethernet.

The chip counts divide exactly into 382 Vera Rubin NVL72 racks, each housing 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs. Neither company disclosed the project's cost, but VR200 NVL72 systems are currently quoted at $5 million to $7 million apiece.

The AI factory follows SoftBank's Blackwell-based DGX supercomputer, announced in 2024, and FugakuNEXT, the $740 million RIKEN, Fujitsu, and Nvidia zetta-scale system due around 2030. Japan's AI Robotics Strategy targets more than 30% of the global AI robotics market by 2040.

No deployment timeline was given in the announcement, but Rubin racks are only expected to reach volume production in the second half of this year. The facility will support trillion-parameter model training 'as the AI factory expands,' suggesting a phased ramp.

The chip counts divide exactly into 382 Vera Rubin NVL72 racks, each housing 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs. Neither company disclosed the project's cost, but VR200 NVL72 systems are currently quoted at $5 million to $7 million apiece.

The AI factory follows SoftBank's Blackwell-based DGX supercomputer, announced in 2024, and FugakuNEXT, the $740 million RIKEN, Fujitsu, and Nvidia zetta-scale system due around 2030. Japan's AI Robotics Strategy targets more than 30% of the global AI robotics market by 2040.
